prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Generate ONE first costume-and-composition study for the KING OF SPADES in this Chinese-inspired playing-card collection. Input 1 is the existing Design 2 blank face FRAME and layout reference. Input 2 is the existing spade PIP, a palette and lotus illustration STYLE reference only, not a shape for the king. A refined flat card illustration, full canvas portrait 5:7, approximately 1060x1484, no mockup.
HISTORICAL COSTUME FOUNDATION: Ming dynasty imperial portrait attire, specifically the museum-described Xuande emperor type: a black gauze YISHANGUAN cap, fitted rounded black front with the two modest wing-like projections folded UPWARD behind it (not long horizontal wings); yellow silk ROUND-COLLAR robe embroidered with Chinese coiling dragon roundels and small clouds, voluminous draped sleeves; red inner collar, a structured belt with rectangular jade/precious-material plaques. A mature Chinese man, dignified calm expression, naturalistic softly shaded face, neatly groomed black moustache and tapered beard. This is an original fictional playing-card sovereign inspired by Ming attire, not a portrait of a named emperor. The black cap replaces a European crown. Do not introduce Qing conical hats, queues, Qing horsehoof cuffs, Japanese armor, fantasy horned headwear, generic European royal clothing, or an ancient bead-curtain crown.
STANDARD CARD POSE: King of Spades with BOTH eyes visible, face gently turned toward the viewer's right. One anatomically natural hand grips an upright straight double-edged Chinese jian-style sword at the viewer's right, blade pointing up beside the shoulder, not behind the head. The other hand rests at his jeweled belt. Keep entire cap and weapon inside the inner frame with breathing room. Show a waist-up figure, not full body.
TWO-WAY COMPOSITION: exactly two opposing waist-up depictions of the SAME man; lower figure is a precise 180-degree ROTATED counterpart of the upper, same face, robe, hands, cap, weapon and ornament. This is rotational symmetry, not a left-right mirror pair and not two upright men. Join the robes at the exact card center with a restrained diagonal woven band and a SMALL central turquoise jewel in a gold lotus rosette, repeating naturally under a half turn. No big divider bar. Faces comfortably separated, hat top near y=13%, upper face near y=24%, belt near midline. Keep generous readable negative space.
STYLE: match input 2's controlled red-and-ivory lotus blooms, teal/verdigris foliage, fine antique gold outlines and rich silk painting. Robe should read as warm imperial yellow with dragon embroidery; restrained madder and teal trim integrate it with the deck. Fine outlines and subtly shaded naturalism, a painted print illustration, not cartoon/anime, plastic 3D or photography. Background is antique white #FAEBD7 with a few small balanced lotus sprigs at the sides; costume and face are the focus.
FRAME: closely retain input 1's narrow black-and-gold lotus-vine band, beaded inner rule, antique-white outer margin, rounded corners, and blank diagonal index panels. Place a clean black serif K above a small plain black spade in the upper-left panel and an exactly rotated copy in the lower-right panel. No other letters or labels. No extra limbs, huge flowers covering anatomy, throne, scenery, caption, watermark, or card-stack mockup. One complete card image for visual review.
